cost of living = the amount of money needed for basic everyday expenses
economic growth = an increase in the amount of goods and services an economy produces
black market = illegal trade in goods or currencies that are banned or rationed
fiscal policy = government decisions on tax and public spending
monetary policy = how a central bank controls money supply and borrowing costs
secular = not connected with religion; keeping religion out of public institutions
poverty = the state of not having enough money for a decent standard of living
inequality = an unfair difference in wealth, rights or opportunities
discrimination = unfair treatment of people because of who they are
civil rights = the rights of citizens to political and social freedom and equality
NGO = a non-governmental organisation that works independently of the state
volunteering = giving your time unpaid to help other people or a cause
charity = an organisation that helps people in need; the act of giving that help
social exclusion = being shut out of the opportunities most people take for granted
social mobility = the ability to move up (or down) the income and class scale
gender equality = equal rights and opportunities for women and men
equal opportunities = the principle that people should compete on a fair basis, without bias
hate crime = a crime motivated by hostility towards a person's identity
xenophobia = dislike or fear of people from other countries
social cohesion = the sense of solidarity and trust that holds a community together
